key_insight: Multimorbidity patterns can be grouped into functional units, and diagnoses connected to more units tend to show faster age-related incidence increases, suggesting shared biology behind chronic disease progression.
clinical_relevance: This work may help explain which chronic diseases are more likely to emerge with age and could point to shared genetic targets relevant for future prevention or therapy research.
method: Analyzed UK Biobank linked health records across 232 diagnoses in 502,355 participants
Used generative representation learning to derive functional units from disease co-occurrence patterns
Compared each diagnosis’s functional-unit breadth with later incidence and supported findings with GWAS, fine-mapping, and external cohorts
evidence_signal: The association between functional-unit breadth and age-dependent incidence was moderate but consistent (Spearman rho = 0.50 overall; 0.4618 in 196 diagnoses with rising hazards), and genetic directionality replicated in FinnGen and the Million Veteran Program.
watch_item: The findings are observational and depend on linked-record coding and cohort composition, so they need prospective validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Functional organization of multimorbidity links chronic disease incidence to shared genetic architecture
